Sam: heads-up, ran a quick perf sweep on the 2-path logic (prefill vs decode) this morning, and i'm seeing a weird crossover where decode kernels beat prefill kernels for mid-length sequences (~160-300) on A100s.
Jia: that's surprising — prefill usually wins up to ~256. Did you change any kernel selection heuristics?
Sam: no config changes, just the recent autotune landing (windowed latency pruning). Suspect the kernel scoring moved some mid-length batches from prefill->decode.
Marta: can you paste the perf numbers? even rough p50/p95 will help.
Sam: p50 tokens/sec (prefill path kernel F32): 3100; decode path kernel BF16-opt: 3300 for 200 tokens. p95 still noisy but looks similar.
Jia: BF16-opt using the new matmul kernel with tile=64? That one has a better memory footprint but worse small-seq startup, so odd it's winning.
Sam: yes tile=64, but note the decode path has fewer KV cache touches when we route because we avoid full prefill KV merge. that reduces memory pressure in this workload.
Marta: aha. so path selection isn't just about raw kernel FLOPs, it's about KV access pattern too. We've assumed prefill path would always be cheaper because it fuses prefill + decode, but KV churn changes that.
Sam: exactly. i ran perf counters: decode path had 30% fewer L2 evictions on these runs. attaching a snippet:
```
# perf sample (summary)
seq_len=200, batch=8
prefill_path: L2_misses=4.2M, gmem_reads=12.3G, latency=62ms
decode_path: L2_misses=2.9M, gmem_reads=9.8G, latency=58ms
```
Jia: interesting. OpsBot note: recent KV cache eviction fix (de-dup window) rolled 2 days ago. Could interact.
Marta: we should consider adding a lightweight heuristic: route mid-length batches to the path that reports lower KV-touch metric at runtime. Something like: if estimated_kv_reads(batch, seq) > threshold -> prefill else decode.
Sam: yeah but estimating KV reads cheaply is the challenge. We can approximate with (batch * prefix_len * head_dim / 64) but that's rough.
Jia: alternative: maintain an LRU-ish telemetry counter for recent batches by seq_bucket; autotuner can pick path per-bucket based on rolling p50 latency + kv_metric. No full historical traces needed.
Marta: sounds good. keep it cheap: one scalar per bucket (recent_score). update with exponential moving average from sampling requests.
Sam: i prototyped something like that: it reduced p50 by ~6% on our internal chat workload. code:
```python
# pseudo: update bucket score on sampled requests
def update_bucket(bucket_id, latency, kv_reads):
    score = latency + kv_reads * 1e-6
    buckets[bucket_id] = alpha * score + (1-alpha) * buckets.get(bucket_id, score)
```
Jia: weights and scaling will be fragile across hardware. We should normalize per-device with a small calibration run on startup.
Marta: agreed. Also add a fallback safety: if a chosen path starts missing SLO we immediately flip to the other for that bucket for N requests.
Sam: logged the experiment as a repeatable perf job (job id 2026-rt-77). I'll attach flamegraphs to the job.
Marta: please add a note for the autotuner: when kernels have similar FLOP estimates, prefer lower-KV path on devices with smaller L2.
Jia: +1. Can we also expose a flag to force path per-model for debugging?
Sam: yep, added a query param `&force_path=prefill|decode` in the test harness.
OpsBot: deploy bot: rolling canary of autotune v2 started in prod-us-west-2 at 2026-03-17T15:02Z.
Marta: ok next steps: (1) Sam — upload perf job + flamegraphs, (2) Jia — sketch the per-bucket EMA logic and calibration routine, (3) me — add SLO flip safety and tie into rollout flags.
Sam: doing that now, will ping when done. :thumbsup:
Jia: i'll get a draft PR for the bucket scoring later today.
Marta: nice work. if we can make the decision data-driven and cheap we can avoid weird regressions when kernels get updated. :100:
perf-bot: sample collector: collected 1200 samples for bucket 3 (seq 128-256) in last 6h.
Sam: that's enough to start. I'll close the loop in this thread when the job finishes.
